prompt:
Edit the supplied own poster into ONE finished flat opaque 16:9 landscape poster. 요청한 화면 비율을 유지하면서 현재 도구와 모델이 지원하는 가능한 최대 해상도로 출력.

Observed repair cause: the returned poster depicts the required actions and readable copy, but uses dense scenic shading, foliage, skyline and fabric detail. Replace that illustration system with the assigned expressive angular drawn frieze. Also reduce the oversized Korean title to fit its intended upper-left area and move the schedule group to its intended start.

Preserve the successful content and information relationships: a continuous left-to-right arrival with a mat, central outdoor film viewing, and right-hand director/audience conversation; one shared creek-bank ground and railing connecting them; warm cream background, vermilion/charcoal palette; Korean title on one complete line with English beneath; date/time/venue together upper right; three arrival entries lower left; programme/weather lower right. Preserve ALL TEN existing text entries exactly once with their spelling, English capitalization, numbers, word spaces and punctuation. Do not add, remove, duplicate or paraphrase any text. Keep the letters crisp and separate from the scene.

Whole drawing change: eliminate the detailed landscape, distant buildings, textured trees, tonal fabric rendering and realistically modelled faces. Reconstruct the same event as a bold contemporary adult arts drawing, using angular bodies built from a few irregular flat planes, bent elbows and knees, small adult-proportioned oval heads, decisive charcoal strokes and selective large vermilion fills. No cute cartoon children, pictorial realism, soft shading, gradients, texture or simulated printing. Flat cream remains visible between and within figures. The adult gestures, overlaps and asymmetric silhouettes drive the lateral movement.

Across x4–96%, roughly y31–69%, show an arriving adult at left visibly unrolling a broad mat, three adults seated on shared mats facing an outdoor film screen at middle, and a standing director turning to two seated adults at right. The director and one audience member clearly exchange a single microphone between them. The last group's gestures open upward. Use a common ground contour and a few simple river-edge railing segments to join the actions as one continuous scene. Suggest the bridge underside with one restrained flat angular beam and pier; suggest water with two decisive creek lines. The screen contains only a sparse bridge-arc and river drawing without any letters. Allow the first two actions to overlap through the shared ground; do not divide them into frames, chapters or panels. Content-grounded illustration must remain substantial and clearly communicate outdoor screening and discussion.

Typography corrections: put “다리 아래 영화관” on ONE complete straight-baseline line entirely inside x4–49%, y5–18%, with a vigorous firm Korean sans around 40–42 px tall at width720; reduce its current width and height accordingly. Put “BRIDGE CINEMA” immediately beneath, around 18–20 px at width720, within the same x4–49% identity area. Move the schedule/venue group's left edge to x52%; retain x52–96%, y6–29%, with stacked date, time and venue. Date/time 23–28 px at width720; venue at least 17 px. Keep clear air between title and schedule. Maintain all remaining text at least 17 px at width720, with straight baselines, comfortable word spaces and intact Hangul counters. Lower-left x4–44%, y73–95% holds the existing three arrival instructions; lower-right x51–96%, y73–95% holds the existing programme descriptor on one line with the weather contingency separately below. Leave the connected middle ground unobstructed.

One independent poster, edge-to-edge opaque cream; no other text, logos, pseudo-print, watermark, QR, signature, mockup, contact sheet or comparison images.
